info.title: Prometheus Backend
info.description:
The JSON/SSE API behind the Prometheus Platform's React frontend. The backend
authenticates users, holds per-browser session state, relays chat turns to the
client-agent orchestrator, and streams progress back over Server-Sent Events.

## Authentication

Authentication is a session cookie (`prometheus_session` by default; the name is
configurable). It is an HttpOnly, `SameSite=Lax` JWT issued by a successful login
and sent automatically by the browser on every request. Routes that need it answer
`401` without a valid, unrevoked cookie; `/api/admin/*` routes additionally answer
`403` unless the user has the `admin` role.

Public routes: `/healthz`, `/.well-known/jwks.json`, `/api/setup/*`, and every
`/api/auth/*` route except `GET /api/auth/me`.

## Typical flow

1. **First run:** `GET /api/setup/status`; if not bootstrapped,
   `POST /api/setup/bootstrap` creates the first admin and logs them in.
2. **Log in:** `GET /api/auth/providers` lists the login options. Then either
   `POST /api/auth/login` (username and password), or follow the browser redirect
   from `GET /api/auth/login/{provider_id}` (OIDC).
3. **Start a conversation:** `POST /api/sessions` binds a new `conversation_id` to
   the session. The id lives server-side and is never sent in a request body.
4. **Open the event stream:** `GET /api/events` (one per browser session) for
   status updates and background-task progress.
5. **Chat:** `POST /api/chat/messages`, optionally attaching files staged with
   `POST /api/uploads`. Fetch artifacts with
   `GET /api/artifacts/{artifact_id}/content`.
6. **History:** `/api/conversations/*` lists, reopens, renames and deletes past
   conversations.

## Errors

Errors are JSON of the form `{"detail": "<message>"}`, and the message is meant to
be shown to the user. The exception is request validation performed by the
framework itself, which returns `422` with `detail` as a list of field errors.

A chat turn that fails while talking to the agent is **not** an HTTP error: it
returns `200` with `status: "error"` and a `message`, so the conversation can render
it inline.

## Wire contract

Every payload is defined by the Pydantic models in `app/contract.py` and explained,
with examples, in `CONTRACT.md` alongside this service.

get.description: ``needs_setup`` is true iff no ``users`` row exists yet.

post.description:
Create the first admin user, once, and log them in immediately.

Closing the race between two concurrent first requests matters here more than
almost anywhere else in the app (it's the one window where *anyone* can create
an admin account) so, on Postgres, this takes a transaction-scoped advisory
lock before checking the count -- a second concurrent request blocks until the
first commits (at which point its own count check correctly sees >0). SQLite
(used in tests, and only in tests) has no advisory locks; the plain
check-then-insert below is fine there since TestClient issues requests
sequentially, not concurrently.
Accept form-encoded or JSON ``{username, password}`` and set the cookie.

identity provider, with the state/nonce cookie ``callback`` reads back.

OIDC redirect callback — resolved through the provider registry (AU-6).

A registered provider completes the handshake via ``IdentityProvider.callback``,
which raises on any failure (``HTTPException`` for a request-level problem,
``NotImplementedError`` for a provider with no redirect flow at all).

get.description:
A turn's state: ``running``, or ``done`` with the response its POST returned.

For a client that lost track of a turn: its POST failed at the network level, or its
event stream reconnected while the turn was in flight. Read once at those moments;
the ``turn_done`` event is the normal path, so don't poll this. 404 when this session
has no such turn (never started, expired, its worker stopped, or another session's).

get.description:
Serve a converted VTP timestep for the React MeshViewer (auth-required).

A mesh artifact's ``json_body.baseUrl`` is ``/api/artifacts/mesh/{dataset_id}``
(see ``services/mesh/service.py``); the viewer fetches each
``${baseUrl}/${filename}`` from here. ``dataset_id`` is a content hash and the
cached files are session-independent, so the guard is auth + path-traversal
safety: both segments must be single safe names and the resolved path must stay
inside the mesh cache root.

post.description:
Rebind the caller's session to a past conversation so the next chat turn
continues it. Returns its transcript + artifact catalog in the same call so
the frontend can render history and resume in one round-trip.

Rebinds first, enriches meshes second. Enrichment can take seconds per mesh on a
cache miss, and the frontend lets the user click elsewhere meanwhile; the rebind
itself is ordered by ``bind_seq`` (see ``SessionStore.reset``), so a newer click
always wins regardless of which request finishes last. The enriched catalog is then
written back only if the session is still on this conversation, with the catalog
the rebind seeded.

AdminUserUpdate.title: AdminUserUpdate
AdminUserUpdate.description: Partial update -- every field is optional; only the ones sent are applied.

ArtifactMeta.title: ArtifactMeta
ArtifactMeta.description:
Conversation-scoped artifact reference on our wire.

Snake_case per the Prometheus catalog convention (see
docs/docs/dev-docs/artifacts.md). Superset of ``prometheus_api``'s
``ArtifactReference`` fields the frontend needs, plus the derived
``render_hint``. ``json_body`` is inline-only; bytes are fetched via
``GET /api/artifacts/{artifact_id}/content`` (task 07).

ChatMessageRequest.title: ChatMessageRequest
ChatMessageRequest.description:
Frontend → backend body for ``POST /api/chat/messages``.

Mirrors the args ``A2AClient.send()`` accepts (frontend/utils/a2a_client.py:81).
``conversation_id`` is **not** in the body — it comes from session state.

ChatMessageResponse.title: ChatMessageResponse
ChatMessageResponse.description:
backend → frontend body for ``POST /api/chat/messages``.

A normalized view of ``prometheus_api``'s ``ConversationResponse``. Fields are
grouped by the ``status`` that populates them; all are optional so a single
model round-trips every variant.

ChatProfile.title: ChatProfile
ChatProfile.description:
A selectable chat profile, mirroring Chainlit's ``cl.ChatProfile``.

Ported from ``frontend/main.py`` ``set_chat_profiles``. The frontend picks one
at session creation; ``POST /api/sessions`` echoes the chosen ``profile`` and,
for the beginner profile, includes ``workflow_suggestions``.

ChatStatus.title: ChatStatus
ChatStatus.description:
Public status set, mirroring ``prometheus_api``'s ``ConversationStatus``.

String-valued so ``response.status == "completed"`` comparisons work on both
sides of the wire.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description:
Source / section / page for a ``reference`` (citation) artifact.

Ported from the old inline citation renderer ``_render_reference_artifact``
(frontend/components/message_handler.py:1004), which read these from the raw
artifact ``metadata``. The frontend's citation card formats from these fields;
without them a ``reference`` artifact loses its provenance on the wire (CON-1).
(The ``uri`` link and ``name``/``description`` the old renderer also used are
already top-level :class:`ArtifactMeta` fields.)

ConversationDetailResponse.title: ConversationDetailResponse
ConversationDetailResponse.description:
Returned by ``GET /api/conversations/{id}`` and ``POST
/api/conversations/{id}/resume`` — a past conversation's transcript plus
enough session-bootstrap info for the frontend to resume it.

ConversationHistoryResponse.title: ConversationHistoryResponse
ConversationHistoryResponse.description:
Returned by ``GET /api/conversations/recent``.

``available`` is ``False`` when Redis is unreachable — the endpoint degrades to
an empty list with a 200 rather than erroring (parallels the Chainlit "History
unavailable" message).

ConversationMessage.title: ConversationMessage
ConversationMessage.description:
One normalized chat turn, as returned by the conversation-detail/resume
endpoints. Distinct from the richer live ``ChatMessageResponse``: this is a
display-only replay of a past turn, not a re-playable turn result.

ConversationResumeRequest.title: ConversationResumeRequest
ConversationResumeRequest.description:
Optional body for ``POST /api/conversations/{id}/resume``.

``bind_seq`` orders session rebinds by click, not by arrival: a resume or new
session whose seq is not greater than the last one applied leaves the session where
it is. The frontend sends a strictly increasing value (``Date.now()``-based).
``POST /api/sessions`` takes the same field in :class:`CreateSessionRequest`.

ConversationSummary.title: ConversationSummary
ConversationSummary.description:
One recent-conversation row.

Mirrors the dict shape produced by
``ConversationStateClient.get_conversation_history`` (ported from the Chainlit
``/history`` command); ``status`` is the client's inferred user-facing status.
``title`` is the effective title: a user rename wins over the client-agent's
LLM-generated title, which wins over the raw first query (``query``).
``pending`` is true while a turn is actively running against this
conversation (``agent:status:{id}.final is False``) — a conversation the
caller isn't currently viewing may still have work in flight.

ConversationTasksResponse.title: ConversationTasksResponse
ConversationTasksResponse.description:
Returned by ``GET /api/conversations/{id}/tasks``: the conversation's Task
Graph as a tree of root turns, newest first. Includes finished tasks until their
nodes expire (24 h by default); filter on ``state`` / ``is_background`` client-side.

``available`` is ``False`` when Valkey is unreachable, matching ``recent``.

CreateSessionRequest.title: CreateSessionRequest
CreateSessionRequest.description:
Optional body for ``POST /api/sessions`` — the selected chat profile, plus the
``bind_seq`` that orders this rebind against in-flight resumes (see
:class:`ConversationResumeRequest`).

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Human-readable explanation, suitable for showing to the user.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Body of every error the backend raises itself.

FormField.title: FormField
FormField.description:
A single follow-up form field.

Matches the props consumed by ``frontend/src/components/chat/FollowupForm.tsx``
and the normalized shape produced by ``normalize_followup_questions`` below
(ported from ``message_handler._handle_needs_info``).

OidcProviderUpdate.title: OidcProviderUpdate
OidcProviderUpdate.description:
Partial update -- every field optional. ``client_secret`` omitted keeps
the existing one; ``provider_id`` isn't editable at all (see module docstring).

TaskNodeOut.title: TaskNodeOut
TaskNodeOut.description:
One Task Graph node, as returned by ``GET /api/conversations/{id}/tasks``.

Mirrors the client-agent's ``TaskNode`` (agents/client-agent/task_graph.py), minus
``conversation_id`` (the request's scope) and ``child_task_ids`` (replaced by the
nested ``children``). A root is one chat turn; its children are the specialist
skill dispatches it made. ``state`` is the effective state after the children
percolate up (an A2A ``TaskState`` string: ``submitted``, ``working``,
``input-required``, ``completed``, ``failed``, ``canceled``, ``rejected``);
``own_state`` is the node's own. ``is_background`` marks a turn the client-agent
detached, and the skill that asked for it. Timestamps are ISO-8601 strings.

TurnStateResponse.title: TurnStateResponse
TurnStateResponse.description:
``GET /api/chat/turns/{turn_id}``: a turn's state, for a client that lost track of it
(POST failed at the network level, or its event stream reconnected).

UploadDescriptor.title: UploadDescriptor
UploadDescriptor.description: Returned by ``POST /api/uploads``; echoed back in the next chat request.

User.title: User
User.description:
Authenticated principal, mirroring Chainlit's ``cl.User`` shape.

``identifier`` matches what the React app read from ``/user``; ``role`` and
``provider`` mirror the ``cl.User.metadata`` keys set in ``auth_callback``.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness probe for load balancers and orchestrators.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Public signing keys (JWKS) that agents use to verify the short-lived identity tokens the backend mints for each chat turn.

tags.name: setup
tags.description: First-run bootstrap: check whether the platform has an admin yet and create the first one. Unauthenticated, and closed for good once any user exists.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Log in with a username and password or an OIDC provider, log out, and identify the current user. Login sets the session cookie.

tags.name: config
tags.description: Settings the UI reads at startup: chat profiles, intro text, suggestions and the upload size limit.

tags.name: sessions
tags.description: Start a new conversation and bind it to the browser session.

tags.name: chat
tags.description: Send a chat turn to the agent orchestrator. Progress for the turn streams over `GET /api/events`.

tags.name: events
tags.description: The per-session Server-Sent Events stream: turn status updates and background-task progress and completion.

tags.name: uploads
tags.description: Stage files to attach to the next chat turn.

tags.name: artifacts
tags.description: Download artifact content produced by agents, and converted mesh files for the 3D viewer.

tags.name: conversations
tags.description: Conversation history: list recent conversations, reopen, resume, rename and delete them.

tags.name: admin-users
tags.description: Manage local user accounts and roles. Requires the `admin` role.

tags.name: admin-oidc-providers
tags.description: Configure the OIDC identity providers offered at login. Requires the `admin` role.

tags.name: admin-signing-keys
tags.description: Create, activate and retire the RS256 keys that sign per-turn identity tokens. Requires the `admin` role.

tags.name: agent-registry
tags.description: Agent self-registration and the A2A gateway the orchestrator calls agents through. Authenticated with the shared agent secret, not the session cookie.
